> ## Types of Simulation. Part 1
>
> From conversation with Gemini on [Types of Simulation (Part 1)](https://share.google/aimode/tOklizJTuSQVKuNa7)
>
> What types of simulation are possible for a simulation tool? List all possible types  (e.g., structural FEA, fluids CFD, or rigid-body physics, etc.)
>
> Engineering simulation tools leverage various numerical methods to represent the physical world. Modern engineering software groups these capabilities into specialized physics domains, individual analysis subtypes, and generative optimization workflows. 
>  - [Simulation Software for Engineering Analysis & Optimization](https://www.3ds.com/technologies/simulation-software)
>  - [Simulation tools for additive manufacturing (AM)](https://www.sintef.no/en/expert-list/sintef-industry/materials-and-nanotechnology/simulation-tools-for-additive-manufacturing-am/)
>
>
> ### 1. Structural Mechanics (FEA - Finite Element Analysis)
>
> Evaluates how solids and structures respond to force, pressure, acceleration, and physical constraints.
>
> - **Static Analysis**: Computes stress, strain, and displacement under constant, time-invariant loads.
> - **Dynamic & Transient Analysis**: Simulates time-dependent behavior such as drop tests, impacts, shock waves, and high-velocity crashes.
> - **Modal & Frequency Analysis**: Identifies the natural resonant frequencies and mode shapes of a structure to avoid structural resonance.
> - **Harmonic & Random Vibration Analysis**: Predicts structural responses to continuous cyclical vibrations (like an engine mount) or random acoustic noise (like a rocket launch).
> - **Fatigue & Durability Analysis**: Predicts structural lifespans and tracks crack initiation under repeated cyclic loading over millions of cycles.
> - **Linear vs. Non-linear Analysis**: Differentiates between predictable materials with minor deflections (linear) and complex events involving plastic deformation, hyperelastic materials (rubber), or buckling (non-linear).
>
> ### 2. Fluid Dynamics (CFD - Computational Fluid Dynamics)
>
> Models the behavior, velocity, pressure, and interaction of gases and liquids as they pass through or around boundaries.
>
> - **Incompressible Flow**: Simulates fluids where density variations are negligible (e.g., low-speed aerodynamics, water flowing through internal piping).
> - **Compressible Flow**: Captures high-velocity fluid dynamics where changes in density are critical, including transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic aerospace vehicles.
> - **Laminar & Turbulent Modeling**: Resolves smooth fluid layers versus complex, chaotic vortices using mathematical turbulence closures (e.g., RANS, LES, DES).
> - **Multiphase Flow**: Tracks the behavior of multiple mixing or unmixing phases, such as liquid-gas boiling, cavitation, or oil-water separation.
> - **Particle Tracking & Discrete Phase**: Simulates solid particulates suspended within a fluid stream, useful for cyclone separators or pollutant dispersion.
>
> ### 3. Thermal & Thermodynamic Analysis
>
> Tracks thermal energy movement, dissipation, and corresponding temperature fields across components.
>
> - **Conduction, Convection, & Radiation**: Models the three fundamental modes of heat transfer through solid contacts, fluid movements, or electromagnetic waves.
> - **Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT)**: Directly couples fluid convection with solid conduction to evaluate cooling efficiency, such as in microchip heatsinks or battery pack cooling.
> - **Thermomechanical Analysis**: Solves thermal expansions and gradients to calculate secondary physical stresses or structural warp caused by intense temperature shifts.
>
> ### 4. Kinematics & Multi-Body Dynamics (MBD)
>
> Simulates interconnected mechanical systems and joints where individual component movements take priority over material deformations.
>
> - **Rigid-Body Dynamics**: Evaluates velocity, acceleration, and driving torques of absolute rigid parts connected by geometric joints (hinges, sliders, balls).
> - **Flexible Multi-Body Dynamics**: Integrates elastic solid elements directly into moving mechanisms to map real-time structural flex during high-speed mechanical cycles.
> - **Vehicle Dynamics**: Specialized templates modeling full chassis mechanics, tire-to-road friction models, suspension physics, and active steering systems.
>
> ### 5. Electromagnetics (EM) & High-Frequency Fields
>
> Predicts the interactions and constraints of electric and magnetic fields within and surrounding operational components.
>
> - **Low-Frequency Electromagnetics**: Simulates electromechanical energy conversion in electric motors, alternators, transformers, and heavy solenoids.
> - **High-Frequency Electromagnetics**: Analyzes signal integrity, wave propagation, radar signatures, antennas, and parasitic capacitance on high-speed printed circuit boards (PCBs).
>
> ### 6. Multiphysics & Specialized Domains
>
> Couples disparate physical regimes simultaneously when isolated single-physics engines yield incomplete data.
>
> - **Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI)**: Dynamically couples fluid pressures to solid surfaces, simulating flapping aerodynamic wings, vascular blood flow, or wind-induced bridge oscillations.
> - **Acoustics & Aeroacoustics**: Models how structural vibrations generate noise (e.g., speakers) or how turbulent fluid fields propagate sound waves (e.g., wind noise around a car side mirror).
> - **Optics & Photonics**: Traces physical light propagation, refractive lens aberrations, and laser interaction profiles.
> - **Chemical Kinetics & Process Simulation**: Models chemical reaction paths, phase changes, mixing loops, and fluid transformations inside industrial reactors.
>
> ### 7. Optimization & Algorithmic Design
>
> Generative simulation routines that systematically evaluate iterations to output an idealized geometric design.
>
> - **Topology Optimization**: Uses structural FEA feedback to systematically strip dead mass away from a design footprint, generating organic, lightweight structures optimized for physical load paths.
> - **Parametric & Shape Optimization**: Mutates user-defined CAD variables (like thickness, radii, or lengths) to satisfy specified physical objectives or safety margins.

## Result

To implement the first batch of simulation types as production-ready features, you must **configure a unified, pipeline-driven architecture where each simulation type is treated as a modular plugin**. Instead of building monolithic software silos, each feature reuse common infrastructural components (like **CAD interaction**, **meshing infrastructure**, and **GPU display** loops) while providing specialized **solvers**, **data structures**, and custom **shaders**.

Here is the comprehensive implementation guide for turning every simulation domain and subtype from Batch 1 into a decoupled app feature.

### 1. Structural Mechanics (FEA) Feature Suite

This suite maps 3D solid continuum geometry to mechanical stress fields. The mathematical objective across these features is solving variations of the structural equilibrium equation: \([M]\{\ddot{u}\} + [C]\{\dot{u}\} + [K]\{u\} = \{F\}\).

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Mesh Strategy**: Continuous solid geometries are converted into conformal volumetric meshes using 10-node quadratic tetrahedral elements (\(Tet10\)) for high-curvature regions or 8-node hexahedral elements (\(Hex8\)) for uniform structural components.

- **Boundary Conditions (BC) Interface**: The UI exposes a **raycasting engine** allowing users to select **geometric faces**, **edges**, or **vertices** to attach **directional load vectors** (\(N\)), **pressure fields** (\(Pa\)), or **absolute displacement constraints** (\(u_x, u_y, u_z = 0\)).

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

```
STRUCTURAL FEA PIPELINE
                                
 ┌──────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
 │ Geometry Selection│ ──►│ Mesh Generation │ ──►│ Stiffness Matrix [K]   │ ──►│ Sparse Solver   │
 └──────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └────────────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
                                                    │                                  │
                                                    ▼                                  ▼
                                         Boundary Conditions (BCs)             Displacements {u}
                                         (Fixed Faces & Load Forces)                   │
                                                                                       ▼
                                                                              Strain & Stress Arrays
                                                                                       │
                                                                                       ▼
                                                                              WebGL/WebGPU Renderer
```

- **Static Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Solves the simplified linear equation \([K]\{u\} = \{F\}\). It drops the mass matrix \([M]\) and damping matrix \([C]\). Uses a direct sparse solver (e.g., PARDISO or a sparse Cholesky decomposition) to solve for displacement vector \(\{u\}\).
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Derives the strain tensor from displacement fields, calculates the Von Mises yield criterion scalar array, and forwards it to a WebGL/WebGPU vertex attribute buffer. A custom fragment shader maps these scalars to an RGB rainbow or viridis color ramp to display structural hot spots.
- **Dynamic & Transient Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Retains time-dependent parameters. Implements an implicit Newmark-\(\beta \) or explicit central-difference time integration scheme. The core solver iterates through discrete time-steps (\(\Delta t\)), tracking momentum transfers, localized velocity profiles, and shockwave propagation across the continuous mesh.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: The asset cache manager streams frames to the visualization layer. The mesh renderer dynamically updates vertex positions in real-time according to a calculated scale factor, allowing users to play back high-speed animations of structural impacts, drops, or crashes.

- **Modal & Frequency Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Computes the free, undamped vibration profile by reducing the core equation down to its generalized eigenvalue problem: \(([K] - \omega^2[M])\{\phi\} = \{0\}\). Uses the Lanczos algorithm to extract the lowest \(N\) eigenvalues (\(\omega \), natural frequencies) and corresponding eigenvectors (\(\{\phi\}\), mode shapes).
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: The UI presents a dropdown listing found resonant frequencies (Hz). Selecting a frequency updates the 3D canvas with an active sinusoidal vertex-deformation loop that visualizes that specific mode's structural shape oscillation.
- **Harmonic & Random Vibration Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: For Harmonic, the solver models continuous sinusoidal excitation by transforming equations into the frequency domain. For Random Vibration, it processes a Power Spectral Density (PSD) input stream over a wide frequency spectrum, utilizing a modal superposition engine to output statistical 1-sigma, 2-sigma, and 3-sigma maximum stress thresholds.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Integrates interactive 2D line charts directly beside the 3D scene graph, letting users click on any 3D node to view its response amplitude curve across the tested frequency bands.

- **Fatigue & Durability Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Operates as a post-processing pass over structural stress cycles. It loops through transient frame arrays, runs a rainflow-counting algorithm to isolate stress ranges, and applies Miner's linear damage rule against material-specific S-N curves (Stress vs. Cycles-to-failure) pulled from the infrastructure layer's database.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Renders a specialized logarithmic contour heatmap highlighting expected component lifespans in cycles alongside critical locations where micro-cracks are predicted to form.

- **Linear vs. Non-linear Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Linear constructs and solves the global stiffness matrix \([K]\) once. Non-linear implements a Newton-Raphson iterative solver to recalculate and reform the tangent stiffness matrix \([K(u)]\) inside every step. This accommodates non-linear material plasticity schemas (like bilinear hardening equations), large geometric deflections (such as buckling), or dynamic changing contact faces between independent meshes.

### 2. Fluid Dynamics (CFD) Feature Suite

This **engine** tracks how continuous fluids move past boundaries. It **solves** the **Navier-Stokes mass and momentum conservation partial differential equations**.

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Mesh Strategy**: Implements automated fluid domain bounding boxes. It generates continuous finite-volume Cartesian grids or unstructured polyhedral meshes, incorporating highly dense, tightly packed mesh layers immediately adjacent to solid faces to resolve boundary layer physics.
- **Boundary Conditions (BC) Interface**: Allows users to mark faces as fluid boundaries: Velocity Inlets (speed vectors), Pressure Outlets (static gauge pressures), or solid, impermeable Walls (enforcing a strict no-slip velocity condition).

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

- **Incompressible Flow**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Assumes constant fluid density (\(\nabla \cdot \vec{u} = 0\)). Employs pressure-velocity coupling schemes such as SIMPLE or PISO to solve velocity and pressure fields while maintaining mass conservation.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: The visualization layer implements vector fields. It draws 3D directional arrow arrays on an slice plane or applies a Line Integral Convolution (LIC) shader to convert raw fluid data into highly readable 2D vector layouts.
- **Compressible Flow**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Couples mass, momentum, and total energy equations to track density shifts (\(\rho = f(P, T)\)) through the Ideal Gas Law. Utilizes density-based solvers optimized to track fluid shocks, choking conditions, and expansion waves.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Shaders calculate the Mach number gradient field, rendering high-contrast Schlieren-style visualization visuals to explicitly expose supersonic shock fronts.
- **Laminar & Turbulent Modeling**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: For low-velocity laminar flows, it resolves raw Navier-Stokes directly. For turbulent flows, it plugs closure models into the solver pipeline: Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS via \(k-\epsilon\) or \(k-\omega\) SST models) for steady-state efficiency, or Large Eddy Simulation (LES) filters to compute complex transient eddies directly.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Extracted scalar matrices map turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) or vorticity values to transparent volume rendering shaders, highlighting chaotic recirculation zones and wake structures.

- **Multiphase Flow**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Integrates tracking interfaces such as the Volume of Fluid (VOF) model or the Level Set method. The solver tracks a phase fraction variable (\(\alpha \)) within every discrete cell, computing changing surface tensions and tracking sharp liquid-gas boundaries over time.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Uses custom isosurface rendering techniques, generating a clear 3D surface mesh exactly where \(\alpha = 0.5\) to depict splashing liquids or boiling bubbles.
- **Particle Tracking & Discrete Phase**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Composes an Eulerian-Lagrangian hybrid pipeline. The fluid phase is computed on the standard continuous mesh (Eulerian framework), while millions of discrete particulate items are tracked through space via distinct kinematic force balance equations (Lagrangian framework).
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Renders particles as instanced GPU primitives, dynamically updating their colors based on individual droplet diameters, velocities, or lifetimes.

### 3. Thermal & Thermodynamic Analysis Feature Suite

Computes the **generation, absorption, and transfer of heat fields**. This operates on a **single scalar Degree of Freedom (DoF)** per **mesh node**: Temperature (\(T\)).

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Mesh Strategy**: Reuses structural FEA solid meshes or CFD volume grids, utilizing matching nodal spacing to simplify cross-physics data mapping.
- **Boundary Conditions (BC) Interface**: Custom UI panels to assign absolute Temperatures (\(K\) or \({}^{\circ }C\)), Heat Flux inputs (\(W/m^2\)), Convective Coefficients (\(h\)), or ambient Radiation environments.

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

- **Conduction, Convection, & Radiation**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Assembles the thermal conductivity matrix. Conduction is computed through solid cell linkages; Convection is modeled as an empirical boundary equation mapping heat drop across surface faces; Radiation uses View Factor calculation matrices to compute Stefan-Boltzmann radiative exchanges across exposed surfaces.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Generates absolute temperature fields. Uses smooth, linear color interpolation across the 3D element faces to display steady-state heat distributions.
- **Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT)**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Couples the solid thermal conduction matrix directly with the fluid CFD solver matrix along shared boundary layers. At every solver iteration loop, the fluid solver transfers computed convection pressures as local wall temperatures, and the solid solver updates with calculated heat rejection back to the fluid.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: The visualization engine uses synchronized split rendering, drawing solid material temperature gradients concurrently alongside fluid stream heat vectors.
- **Thermomechanical Analysis**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Implements a two-pass sequential multiphysics pipeline. Pass 1 solves the thermal equation to get a nodal temperature field array \(\Delta T\). Pass 2 feeds this \(\Delta T\) array directly into the Structural FEA engine as an initial load vector, using the material's thermal expansion coefficient (\(\alpha \)) to compute structural warping, thermal stresses, and deformations.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Renders the deformed shape layout overlaying the original geometry, using a dual heatmap system showing thermal values and mechanical stress zones simultaneously.

### 4. Kinematics & Multi-Body Dynamics (MBD) Feature Suite

Simulates the **kinematics** of **complex mechanical assemblies**, prioritizing **full component movement** and **inter-part connection logic** over **internal material elastic deformation**.

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Mesh Strategy**: Skips volumetric continuum meshing entirely. Parts are treated as rigid, solid bodies defined purely by global center-of-mass coordinates, total mass values, and full Inertia Tensors (\(I_{xx}, I_{yy}, I_{zz}\)).
- **Boundary Conditions (BC) Interface**: The layout setup uses a mechanical constraint manager. Users click on mating features to instantiate Joints (Revolute/Hinge, Prismatic/Slider, Cylindrical, or Ball joints) and apply driving forces or rotational motor velocities.

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

```
MULTI-BODY DYNAMICS PIPELINE
                           
 ┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
 │ Rigid Components│ ──►│ Joint Matrix    │ ──►│ ODE/DAE Solver    │ ──►│ Coordinate      │
 │ Mass & Inertia  │    │ Constraint Links│    │ (Forward Euler/   │    │ Transform Matrix│
 └─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘    │  Newmark-alpha)   │    └────────┬────────┘
                                               └───────────────────┘             │
                                                                                 ▼
                                                                        Scene Graph Node Upd.
                                                                        (Smooth 3D Motion)
```

- **Rigid-Body Dynamics**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Forms equations of motion as a system of Index-3 Differential-Algebraic Equations (DAEs). Resolves constraints via Lagrange multipliers, computing forward integrations using implicit solvers (like HHT-\(\alpha \)) to calculate velocities, acceleration vectors, and reaction forces at every joint constraint.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Bypasses vertex buffer regeneration. The orchestration core directly updates the model transformation matrix (\(4\times4\) position/rotation matrices) of the relevant 3D scene graph nodes, allowing smooth 60fps rendering of mechanical paths.

- **Flexible Multi-Body Dynamics**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: Integrates localized elasticity by utilizing Component Mode Synthesis (CMS) or Craig-Bampton reduction. This blends small, reduced-order linear FEA substructures into the rigid dynamic movement pipeline, allowing specific parts to flex and bend during rapid mechanical movements.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Uses dynamic vertex buffers on flexible components to display local stresses caused by high-speed inertial impacts while maintaining rigid parent coordinate movement.

- **Vehicle Dynamics**:
  - **Solver Configuration**: A specialized configuration package incorporating analytical sub-models: non-linear tire road friction formulas (Pacejka Magic Formula), active damper curves, steering rack linkages, and anti-roll bar systems.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Renders real-time telemetry overlays, plotting slip angles, body roll centers, and suspension stroke metrics next to a chasing camera viewport tracking the virtual vehicle.

### 5. Electromagnetics (EM) Feature Suite

Tracks **electric and magnetic field interactions** by **solving** **Maxwell’s partial differential equations**.

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Mesh Strategy**: Utilizes specialized Nedelec edge-element vector meshes (rather than standard node-based setups) to preserve electric and magnetic field continuity across material boundaries. Includes an explicit "Air Box" mesh enclosing the physical 3D model to capture surrounding free-space field propagation.
- **Boundary Conditions (BC) Interface**: Controls to declare current ports, voltage sources, coils, perfect electrical conductors (PEC), or absorbing boundary conditions (ABC) to isolate the outer air perimeter.

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

- **Low-Frequency Electromagnetics**
  - **Solver Configuration**: Solves quasi-static Maxwell setups where displacement current terms are dropped. Focuses heavily on magnetic vector potential formulations to calculate eddy currents, magnetic flux saturation, and reluctance in iron cores.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Shaders generate 3D magnetic flux lines using animated tube or streamline primitives, mapping the local magnetic flux density (\(B\) field) to a distinct color gradient across motor stators and rotors.
- **High-Frequency Electromagnetics**
  - **Solver Configuration**: Full Maxwell equation solver utilizing Finite Element Frequency Domain (FEFD) or Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) schemes. Computes full scattering parameters (S-parameters), antenna radiation patterns, and wave attenuation profiles across high-speed PCB layouts.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: Computes far-field radiation properties, rendering interactive 3D polar radiation lobes mapped over the physical antenna geometry.

### 6. Multiphysics & Specialized Domains

Orchestrates communication loops between **distinct**, **separate** **solver engines** when isolated **single**-**physics** **configurations** are insufficient.

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Orchestration Framework**: Uses a dedicated synchronization bus within the Application Core. It supports weak coupling (staggered, iterative data passing between individual solvers per step) and strong coupling (assembling different physical variables into one unified global matrix solved simultaneously).

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

- **Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI)**:
  - **Architecture Implementation**: Connects the CFD and Structural FEA solvers. Fluid pressure arrays acting on solid boundaries are extracted from the CFD solver, translated across mismatched meshes using a radial basis function (RBF) mapping pipeline, and passed to the structural engine as surface forces. The structural engine solves for deformation and updates the boundary geometry coordinates back inside the CFD engine for the next cycle.
  - **Acoustics & Aeroacoustics**:
    - **Architecture Implementation**: For structural acoustics, structural mesh vibrations compute sound pressure propagation through Helmholtz wave solvers. For **Aeroacoustics**, transient fluid vortices computed by a high-fidelity LBM fluid engine are converted into acoustic source terms using Lighthill’s acoustic analogy to model aerodynamic wind noise.
  - **Optics & Photonics**:
    - **Architecture Implementation**: Implements ray-tracing or wave-optics algorithms. Tracks electromagnetic wavefronts passing through refracting mediums, computing optical path distortions caused by thermal or structural changes in lenses.
  - **Chemical Kinetics & Process Simulation**:
    - **Architecture Implementation**: Extends the CFD fluid pipeline with mass transport conservation equations. Tracks individual species concentration fields, resolving localized volumetric chemical reactions and phase shifts at each cell node.

### 7. Optimization & Algorithmic Design Feature Suite

An automated workflow layer that wraps around the simulation engines to iteratively mutate design geometries based on mathematical goals.

#### Implementation Architecture

- **Automation Framework**: Operates as an algorithmic loop controlled by the Core Orchestration layer. It executes simulations automatically, extracts result metrics, processes sensitivity analyses, modifies design inputs, and reruns the entire loop until convergence criteria are met.

#### Subtype Feature Implementations

```
GENERATIVE OPTIMIZATION LOOP
                         
┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌────────────────┐
│ Initial CAD/Mesh│ ──►│ Run Physics FEA │ ──►│ Evaluate Stress  │ ──►│ Sensitivity    │
└─────────────────┘    └────────▲────────┘    │ & Mass Targets   │    │ Analysis Block │
                        │                     └────────┬─────────┘    └────────┬───────┘
                        │                              │                       │
                        │ No                           ▼                       ▼
                        └──────────────────────  Convergence?  ◄─────────── Remove Mass /
                                                       │                    Mutate CAD
                                                       ▼ Yes
                                                Optimized Design
```

- **Topology Optimization**:
  - **Architecture Implementation**: Implements the SIMP (Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization) method. The optimization loop treats the density (\(\rho_e \in [0, 1]\)) of every mesh element as a continuous variable. It runs a structural FEA, tracks the strain energy sensitivity of each element, and strips away material from low-stress zones by driving their density to 0, producing optimized, lightweight biomimetic designs.
  - **Post-Processing & Visualization**: The visualization engine uses a specialized threshold filter shader. It hides all mesh elements where \(\rho_e < 0.3\), dynamically displaying the progressive erosion of dead mass in real time after each design loop.

- **Parametric & Shape Optimization**:
  - **Architecture Implementation**: Links directly to the parametric CAD model data schema. The engine couples optimization algorithms (e.g., **Sequential Quadratic Programming** or **Genetic Algorithms**) to explicit **CAD variables** (like plate thicknesses, hole radii, or slot lengths), mutating those dimensional values systematically to minimize total mass while satisfying factor-of-safety structural targets.

### Summary of App Configuration States for Batch 1

To manage these configurations within your application core cleanly, you can encapsulate each simulation type into a structured state object. This object tells the pipeline which specific tools and solvers to activate:

```typescript
// Unified Type Schema for App Core Feature Management
interface ISimulationFeatureConfig {
  domainId: 'STRUCTURAL' | 'FLUIDS' | 'THERMAL' | 'MBD' | 'EM' | 'MULTIPHYSICS' | 'OPTIMIZATION';
  meshType: 'Solid_Tet10' | 'Volume_Polyhedral' | 'Edge_Nedelec' | 'Rigid_Node' | 'Adaptive_SIMP';
  degreeOfFreedomPerNode: number; // e.g., 3 for Structural (u_x,u_y,u_z), 1 for Thermal (T)
  primarySolverEngine: string;    // e.g., 'Sparse_Cholesky', 'PISO_Coupled', 'HHT_Alpha_ODE'
  vertexShaderId: string;         // Controls 3D visualization mapping (Contour, Streamline, Deformation)
}
```
